**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Chūnqiū jí zhuàn biàn yí* 春秋集傳辨疑 in ten juan is the third of Lù Chún's [陸淳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E6%B7%B3) *Chūnqiū* works (the others being [KR1e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0013) *Zuǎn lì* and [KR1e0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0014) *Wēi zhǐ*) — a sustained polemic against the three commentaries' specific entries which Lù judged unsupportable. The work refutes the *Sān zhuàn* on a phrase-by-phrase basis where the *Zuǎn lì* had only treated the same material as a structured catalog. Liǔ Zōngyuán's [柳宗元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B3%E5%AE%97%E5%85%83) tomb-inscription gives the work as seven *piān* 篇; the present text is ten juan, redivided after the Yuán *Yányòu* 延祐 5 (1318) Jiāngxī xíngshěng 江西行省 imperial recutting at the petition of the Hànlín scholar Kèchóu 克酬.

**Abstract**

The *Sìkù tíyào* makes the principal points: that this work is the polemical complement to the *Zuǎn lì* — the *Zuǎn lì* gives the constructive Dàn–Zhào–Lù programme, the *Biàn yí* lists the negative case against the three commentaries entry by entry; that the work draws more heavily on Zhào Kuāng than on Dàn Zhù; that the *tíyào* itself takes a balanced view, recognising both the work's tendency to over-doubt and the genuine philological precision of its best passages.

The *Biàn yí*'s significance is that, alongside the *Wēi zhǐ*, it is the most fully argued single Táng-period polemical attack on the *Zuǒzhuàn*'s historicity and the *Gōngyáng*/*Gǔliáng*'s exegetical fidelity. Its judgments — whatever one's verdict on individual cases — opened the doctrinal space within which Sòng *xīnyì* commentators could read the *Chūnqiū* directly. Sūn Fù's *Zūn wáng fā wéi* [KR1e0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0018), building explicitly on Lù Chún, takes the same direct-reading line, as do Liú Chǎng [KR1e0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0021) *et seq.* and ultimately Hú Ānguó [KR1e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0036). Without Lù Chún's *Biàn yí*, the Sòng *Chūnqiū xīnyì* movement would have been hermeneutically unintelligible.
